transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

I'm... I'm here because of work. My manager told me I had to come. People got scared because I kept... freezing up. Like, right in the middle of a shift. I guess I was doing things out of order. They said I was just standing by the soda machine holding the cash drawer key, just... repeating table numbers over and over instead of closing out the checks. I don't really know.
Roughly how long do these freezing episodes usually last?
I don't know... I guess I don't really keep track of the time. It's hard to tell.
How do you feel immediately after one of these episodes ends?
I don't know... just tired, I guess. Confused. I just want to go back to work and finish what I was doing.
Do you notice any unusual sensations or warnings right before these episodes happen?
No... not really. I don't think so. It just... happens, I guess. I haven't noticed anything like that.

latest_inference.note: Absence of myoclonic jerks and presence of postictal confusion/fatigue with automatisms makes focal impaired awareness seizures (complex partial seizures, G40.2) the primary diagnosis, ruling out generalized idiopathic epilepsy syndromes such as JME/absence (G40.3).

inference_history.note: Initial presentation of episodic unresponsiveness, automatic behaviors (perseverative repetition, freezing), and lack of awareness/amnesia raises concern primarily for focal impaired awareness seizures (epilepsy), transient global amnesia, dissociative disorders, delirium, or psychotic/catatonic phenomena.

Post-episode confusion and tiredness point toward a post-ictal state characteristic of focal impaired awareness seizures (G40.2). F05 and F20.9 are ruled out due to the paroxysmal nature and clear baseline functioning, while F44.0 is unlikely given classic post-ictal fatigue/confusion. Added G40.3 as a differential paroxysmal seizure disorder.
Ruled out G45.4 due to recurrent brief freezing episodes with post-ictal fatigue and confusion rather than prolonged isolated anterograde amnesia.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient experiences unprovoked, recurring episodes of behavioral arrest ('freezing up') with impaired consciousness and automatisms/perseverative behavior (repeating table numbers, holding keys without purposeful action), followed by post-ictal fatigue and confusion with amnesia for the episodes. This clinical presentation is characteristic of localization-related (focal) epilepsy with complex partial seizures.
